findings.reason: bounding the section's claim to cycles faster than the interval, and choosing the interval with margin over the period's observed variance, changes the sampling constant and the sentence a node builds against; left as written it presents a rate-limited detector as a universal one.
findings.text: §5 asserts its two readings "cannot read the same count on both" and that this is how "a cycle of any cause becomes visible", but that guarantee holds only for a sustained cycle faster than the 10 s interval; §1's period is a single point measurement (restarts 6 in 40 s, about 6.7 s) whose import-time component varies, so a slower pass can push the period past 10 s and both readings can match, reporting the cycling unit healthy — the same false negative §5 exists to remove — while a genuinely slower cycle of any other cause is never seen at all. A reader or builder acting on "any cause" will not build for that case, and the margin is only 1.5x over a figure measured once, so the guard's sufficiency rests on a claim the section's own evidence does not support.
